In 1967, an entire country switched sides of the road. Overnight.
Sweden drove on the left. But all its neighbors drove on the right, and most Swedish cars already had the steering wheel on the left.
In a vote, eighty-three percent of Swedes said no to switching. The government did it anyway.
They called it Dagen H. H for hoger, which means right.
Crews had to swap three hundred and sixty thousand road signs, and keep the new ones covered.
There was even a pop song to help. Keep to the right, Svensson.
On Sunday, September third, almost all traffic was banned. At ten to five in the morning, every car stopped.
Drivers carefully moved over to the other side of the road, and waited.
At exactly five o'clock, Sweden drove off on the right.
And the Monday after, there were fewer crashes than usual. Everyone was driving extra carefully.
